site.name: shopify
site.summary: shopify-clone Clone of the Shopify marketing → trial → admin funnel. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: hero ("Your business starts with Shopify" + email signup input), product features, customer success stories, customer logos, footer | | `pricing.html` | Plan comparison: Basic / Shopify / Advanced three tiers, monthly / yearly toggle, feature comparison table, FAQ | | `free-trial.html` | Trial landing page: 3-step intro to the trial flow, value props restated, large "Start free trial" button |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full shopify system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Shopify onboarding funnel suffers from critical validation and navigation failures that directly block user goal completion. Key conversion flows—such as the hero email form and the login form—lack inline validation and fail to navigate correctly, leaving users without feedback or a clear path forward. Additionally, mobile usability is severely hampered by horizontal overflow, undersized tap targets, and inaccessible form controls.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full Shopify system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by traversing the primary onboarding funnel from the homepage email input through the multi-step trial form to completion. It will then validate adjacent flows including the login, enterprise sales contact form, and pricing toggle interactions. Finally, it will assess content pages, error handling, and mobile responsiveness, paying close attention to the numerous small tap targets and missing input labels identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The multi-step form on free-trial-form.html reveals subsequent steps (location, account creation) interactively via the 'Next' button rather than loading new pages.
The login and sales forms will display inline validation errors when submitted with invalid or empty data.
The monthly/yearly toggle on pricing.html dynamically updates the plan prices and feature details.
Footer links pointing to '#' (e.g., Solutions, About, Careers) are placeholder links and will not navigate to new content.
risk_hotspots: free-trial-form.html: Multi-step form progression, skip functionality, and validation error recovery paths.
sales.html: Missing input labels for phone number and company size fields, which harms accessibility and could confuse users.
admin.html: Login error states and social login (Apple/Google/Facebook) fallback behavior.
pricing.html: Accurate dynamic updating of prices and feature details when toggling between monthly and yearly billing.
Global: Widespread small tap targets in the header, footer, and navigation links, posing a significant mobile UX risk.

phases.title: Primary Onboarding Funnel
phases.objective: Validate the core conversion path from the homepage email input through the multi-step trial signup form.
key_checks: Submit the homepage email form with an invalid format and verify inline error handling.
Submit the homepage email form with a valid email and confirm navigation to free-trial-form.html.
Progress through the 'What are you planning to sell?' step, selecting various options.
Test the 'Skip all' functionality and verify it bypasses remaining steps appropriately.
Complete the multi-step form to the 'Your store is ready!' state, ensuring smooth transitions.
exit_criteria: Successful completion of the trial form to the final success state.
Validation error triggered and displayed for invalid email input.

phases.title: Authentication & Recovery
phases.objective: Test the login flow, including error states, social login options, and navigation to signup.
key_checks: Attempt to log in with empty fields and verify error messaging.
Attempt to log in with invalid credentials and verify error messaging.
Check the 'Forgot password?' link behavior.
Verify navigation from 'New to Shopify? Start free trial' back to the onboarding flow.
exit_criteria: Login validation errors observed for empty and invalid inputs.
Forgot password and signup navigation paths verified.

phases.title: Pricing & Enterprise Contact
phases.objective: Validate the pricing page interactions and the enterprise sales contact form, including accessibility issues.
key_checks: Toggle between 'Pay monthly' and 'Pay yearly' and verify price/feature updates.
Expand FAQ accordions and verify content visibility.
On sales.html, submit the form with empty required fields to trigger validation.
Verify the accessibility and labeling of the company size and topic select dropdowns on sales.html.
Navigate via the 'View pricing' link back to pricing.html.
exit_criteria: Pricing toggle successfully updates plan details.
Sales form validation triggered for empty inputs.
Missing label accessibility issue confirmed on sales.html.

phases.title: Content & Help Pages
phases.objective: Explore the resources and help center pages to ensure navigation and search functionality operate correctly.
key_checks: Verify navigation links to Help Center, Academy, Theme Store, and App Store from resources.html.
Test the search input on help-trial.html.
Click the table of contents links (e.g., 'Initiate the free trial') and verify scroll/navigation behavior.
Verify inline links (e.g., 'sign up for a free trial') navigate correctly.
exit_criteria: Help center search and navigation functioning.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and high-risk areas on a mobile viewport to assess responsiveness and tap target issues.
key_checks: Verify homepage hero and email input adapt properly to mobile viewport.
Assess the multi-step trial form usability on mobile, checking for layout shifts or obscured inputs.
Evaluate the pricing toggle and comparison table readability on mobile.
Confirm the severity of small tap targets identified in the prescan (header nav, footer links).
exit_criteria: Critical flows validated on mobile viewport.
Tap target and layout warnings documented with visual evidence.

coverage_targets.features: exercise all form inputs, validation states, toggles, and key navigation links per page
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, specifically targeting known small tap targets and form usability

notes: free-trial.html appears to be a duplicate of index.html based on the prescan; verify if it behaves differently or is just a variant.
Focus heavily on the missing input labels on sales.html and the small tap targets across the site during the mobile phase.
Several footer links point to '#'; note these as dead ends in the UX critique rather than attempting to navigate them repeatedly.

findings.user_goal: Sign up for a free trial via the homepage hero form
findings.problem: Submitting an invalid or empty email address in the hero form provides no inline validation error, leaving the user unaware of why the submission failed.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Start free trial' button with an empty or invalid email resulted in no visible change or inline validation error. The form lacks client-side inline validation for invalid/empty email inputs.
findings.why_it_matters: Without feedback, users are left confused about the requirements, likely causing them to abandon the signup process entirely.
findings.suggestion: Implement immediate inline validation below the email field to indicate when an email is missing or malformed.

findings.user_goal: Sign up for a free trial via the homepage hero form
findings.problem: The hero form submission fails to navigate the user to the trial form, breaking the primary conversion flow.
findings.evidence: Clicking the hero 'Start free trial' button changed the text to 'Starting...' but the URL remained index.html. Form submission via pressing Enter also failed to navigate to free-trial-form.html.
findings.why_it_matters: A broken primary conversion path prevents users from creating an account, resulting in a total failure of the user's primary goal.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the form submission handler correctly redirects to free-trial-form.html upon successful validation.

findings.problem: The 'Forgot password?' link is a dead link, failing to provide a password recovery flow.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Forgot password?' points to '#', failing to provide a password recovery flow and resulting in a poor UX for users who cannot access their account.
findings.why_it_matters: Users who forget their passwords are completely locked out with no way to recover their accounts, causing frustration and trust issues.
findings.suggestion: Implement a password reset flow or link to an existing recovery page instead of a dead anchor link.

findings.problem: The enterprise contact form submits successfully with empty required fields, displaying a 'Thank you' message instead of validation errors.
findings.evidence: The enterprise contact form submitted successfully with empty required fields, displaying a 'Thank you! Your enquiry has been submitted' message instead of inline validation errors.
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing blank submissions creates false positives for the user and sends unhelpful, empty leads to the sales team, degrading trust on both sides.
findings.suggestion: Add required field validation to prevent form submission until all necessary fields are filled out.

findings.user_goal: Log into an existing store admin
findings.problem: The login form allows submission of empty fields and displays a 'Login successful' message without actually validating credentials.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Log in' with empty fields did not trigger inline validation errors; instead, it bypassed validation and displayed a 'Login successful' message.
findings.why_it_matters: Faking a successful login prevents users from accessing their store while misleading them into thinking their credentials were accepted, causing severe confusion.
findings.suggestion: Implement proper client-side and server-side validation to check for empty fields and correct credentials before authenticating the user.

findings.problem: The country/region select dropdown is missing a label, aria-label, or placeholder, harming accessibility.
findings.evidence: Medium severity UX issue: The country/region select dropdown (ux-4) is missing a label, aria-label, or placeholder, which harms accessibility for screen readers.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not know the purpose of the dropdown, making the form impossible to complete accessibly.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible <label> element or an aria-label attribute to the select dropdown.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the site on a mobile device
findings.problem: The homepage has a horizontal overflow issue on mobile viewports, causing elements to extend beyond the screen width.
findings.evidence: Horizontal overflow detected on mobile viewport (page width 422px exceeds 390px viewport), likely caused by the hero section or input layout.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling creates a disjointed and frustrating mobile experience, potentially obscuring critical content or form inputs.
findings.suggestion: Ensure all container elements and inputs use responsive units (e.g., max-width: 100%, box-sizing: border-box) to prevent overflow.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site on a mobile device
findings.problem: Multiple navigation and footer links have tap targets significantly below the 44px mobile guidance, making them difficult to activate accurately.
findings.evidence: Multiple small tap targets identified in the footer (e.g., 'About', 'Careers' at 342x21px) and header ('Menu' at 20x14px, 'Solutions' at 76x17px), failing the 44px mobile tap target guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets lead to mis-taps and navigation errors, severely degrading the mobile user experience.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around text links to ensure a minimum tap target size of 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Explore resources like the Theme Store or App Store
findings.problem: Several resource links point to '#' instead of dedicated pages, confusing users expecting distinct destinations.
findings.evidence: Several resource links (Shopify Academy, Theme Store, App Store) point to '#' instead of dedicated pages, which could confuse users expecting distinct destinations.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead links disrupt the user's exploration flow and erode trust in the site's reliability.
findings.suggestion: Link resource cards to their corresponding pages or remove the links until the pages are ready.
